basics.name: Jeroen Wever
basics.title: Freelance staff-level full-stack engineer
basics.intro: Freelance staff-level full-stack engineer. I've been building web products people actually use for almost 20 years
basics.tagline: These days with AI agents, while I decide where the bar sits.
basics.summary: I'm a tech junkie with a brain like a pressure cooker: curious, energetic, honest, self-taught. I have an urge to make things, and I've built web products for the Benelux's biggest news and entertainment brands and for real-time sports betting. I have a strong vision of how a development team should work together and I know which roles it takes. Everything I build is meant to stop needing me.

ai: I work agentic first and try to get as close as I can to a lights-off factory: building software without human intervention. I don't think good software can do without people yet, so I start with human gates for product, graphic design, architecture, technical design and code. I turn those into agent gates as time and experience grow, as long as that doesn't introduce major issues.
Whatever can be solved deterministically, I solve deterministically.

experience.summary: Three engagements on TOTO's gambling platforms: a brand integration into the legacy casino, a ground-up rebuild of [the casino](https://casino.toto.nl), and the new [TOTO Sport](https://sport.toto.nl) sportsbook. All real-time, all under strict gambling regulation, peaking at 100,000 active users a night.
highlights: Shipped the Winn-It brand into the legacy casino platform in six weeks, against a six-month budget

Rebuilt the casino from scratch on Vue 3 and .NET, then handed it over to newly hired in-house engineers. The team chose a custom SSR stack over Nuxt: no vendor lock-in, and every engineer learns what a meta-framework does under the hood
Owned the initial SSR implementation for both casino and sportsbook. Researched the hard parts (memory leaks and state leaking across requests) and coached the team on preventing both

Turned a three-month sportsbook proof-of-concept into a green light at the halfway demo. With four engineers, reached closed beta in a year and replaced the legacy product six months later, handling peaks of 4,000 logins and 2,000 bets per minute
Troubleshot the sportsbook in Kubernetes with kubectl, mostly by digging through pod logs. Tuned autoscaling for the evening peaks and sparred on the manifests
Wrote C# in the .NET backend and built the Node and Vue layer that talks to it, so knows both sides of the line between C# and TypeScript
Built the custom Google Analytics enhanced-ecommerce funnel for betting, plus the sportsbook's custom A/B-testing setup. A betslip is not a shopping cart
Made both products webview-ready for the iOS/Android apps, debugging the not-quite-a-browser quirks side by side with the app engineers
Worked with AI as a pair programmer within TOTO's AI policy: the AI implements, I steer and review

experience.summary: Built and ran entertainment products: video, puzzles, casual games, quizzes and podcasts. They served roughly 1.5 billion views a year across DPG's biggest brands (AD, HLN, de Volkskrant), with advertising, paywalls and tracking built in, under a "you build it, you run it" principle.
highlights: Built the embed system end to end: the loader script, the data-attribute element API, and the embeds themselves in vanilla JavaScript, CSS and HTML. Nearly all of it mine, with the team as sparring partners. Carried video from 4 to 20+ titles, then puzzles, games, quizzes and podcasts
Implemented the complete Snowplow analytics integration on the front-end: plays and playthrough, profile-based recommendations, and daily-puzzle notifications that knew whether you'd already played
Built the web side of the "wall" product: a brand sets up one route with its own header and footer, and we render everything in between. One lightweight integration per label
Worked in continuous back-and-forth with the app teams on webview integration; later ported the products to React alongside the React Native apps
Ran what we built: containerized hosting in AWS, caching and WAF in Akamai, monitoring and alerting

experience.summary: Led front-end development (75% hands-on, 25% leading) for a team of about 8 front-end engineers in a fast-paced B2C campaign environment, for clients such as Audi, Renault, Dutch Railways (NS) and the Ministry of Health.
highlights: Stepped into the front-end-lead gap from day one. The sitting lead announced his departure the day I started, so in practice I took on the estimations and the back-and-forth with PMs and traffic
Defined the common front-end stack and coding standards used across projects and teams
Gave a trainee his first production project, trainbooking.com, with direct client contact included, and guided him through it
Encouraged an engineer to take campaign sites to React, then guided him in building our reusable campaign tooling. In effect our own meta-framework, before Next.js existed
Delivered under hard campaign deadlines, including a multilingual Audi site live within four weeks

experience.summary: Started full-stack in the ASP.NET and jQuery era, building business web applications for clients including PostNL, ING, Rijkswaterstaat, KPN, Ziggo and de Persgroep.
highlights: Claimed the front-end spot nobody wanted and grew it into a UX practice: user sessions, client presentations, and sparkling interfaces on top of server-rendered pages
Kept de Persgroep's news platforms running at 35M pageviews a month, a big number in 2010

items: Analytics & experimentation (GA, GTM, Snowplow, A/B testing)
Specifying with tests before an agent starts
Splitting work across building and reviewing agents (Claude Code)
Any language with an expert on the team. I ask, I learn
Translating abstract ideas into structured processes and UX

education.degree: MSc Information Science: Human Centered Multimedia

personal: I just finished the log cabin in my backyard, bathroom and kitchen included, and it's now my little office. My team of three kids and I report to my wife, and I'm over-engineering a meal planner, because deciding at 17:00 what's for dinner is the mental equivalent of driving your car into a ditch. On the side I make [a swipe game about the AI race](https://last-invention.sugarrush.dev) and a scheduling tool for daycare.
